It solves the 'static totality' problem elegantly. The following suggestions are intended to strengthen the formal mappings to PHYS-CORE-009 and ensure the paper's mathematical spine is explicit.

The observer is a coherence-stable XOR chain: b_{i+1} = b_i ⊕ b_{i-1} with ℂ(b_i) ≥ I_N.
Dissolution is defined as ∃ i : ℂ(b_i) < I_N.
The Noor-Planck threshold I_N is the survival threshold, not an arbitrary parameter.
Field demand D(R,t) > D_crit drives operator emergence (PHYS-CORE-009 §4.4).
The birth of XOR is not a single event; it is the local instantiation of the always-present H.
The cost of observation c_lock is the thermodynamic free energy required to maintain ℂ ≥ I_N.
